name: @olai/odu-client
//: HOW OLAI REACHES ODU — see src/index.ts, which argues the whole boundary. What this manifest is FOR is the wall: a package cannot depend back on @olai/server, so the direction is physics rather than discipline. It is @olai/kolu-client's manifest one appliance over, and deliberately the same shape.
//dependencies: It names NO olai package at all, for @olai/kolu-client's reason: the wire vocabulary this package produces lives IN it (src/wire), which `@olai/surface` spreads into its own spec — so the direction is a DAG the manifests enforce (surface → odu-client → nothing). @olai/format is absent for the same reason it is there: the walk over the vault that finds which lanes name a worktree belongs to whoever holds the vault (@olai/server's lanes.ts), and it is INJECTED (OduDeps.lanes) rather than imported. `@odu/run-client` — juspay/odu#94's thin client, the only thing here that knows odu exists — is hydrated as raw TypeScript from a Nix pin (nix/odu.nix) rather than installed from bun.lock, so it is not named here at all and its own declared external (`effect`, at this tree's pinned version) is declared once for the whole tree in the root package.json. scripts/check-odu-deps.sh keeps that honest AND confines it: its second assertion greps packages/*/src and allows an `@odu/*` specifier in this package alone, with zero exceptions; its third keeps ./wire pure — no @odu, no solid-js, no format, no node: — because @olai/surface spreads that entry and every listener pulls it in statically.
